records.quote: Theorem 2. Let X1 , . . . , Xn be independent random variables with Xi ∼ Fré(µ, θi , α), i = 1, . . . , n, and Y1 , . . . , Yn be independent random variables with Yi ∼ Fré(µ, θi∗ , α), i = 1, . . . , n. If ( 1/θ1 , . . . , 1/θn ) ≽w ( 1/θ1∗ , . . . , 1/θn∗ ), then Xn:n ≥rh Yn:n .
records.family: Fréchet Fré(µ, θi, α); common location µ and shape α, heterogeneous scales θi vs θi*
records.compared: reciprocal scale vectors (1/θi) under the paper's weak majorization ≽w

hypotheses.formal: paper-defined weak majorization on reciprocal scales (this paper's ≽w = 'weakly supermajorizes' convention of its Definition, i.e. reciprocal-scale vector of X weak upper majorizes that of Y)

hypotheses.text: common location µ and common shape α

conclusion.direction: Xn:n >=rh Yn:n (reversed hazard rate; r̃Xn:n >= r̃Yn:n)

records.ambiguity: Hypothesis is on reciprocals 1/θi (rendered as '( θ1 , . . . , θ1n )' in the text layer). This paper's ≽w convention ('weak upper majorization' on partial sums of smallest components) corresponds to Marshall–Olkin weak submajorization; kept as printed. Generalizes Gupta et al.'s Theorem 2 from ≤st to ≥rh.

note: Order label dispute resolved to rh (printed ≥rh; A's record body already said rh — only its order tag read 'hr'). Direction Xn:n >=rh Yn:n agreed by both passes; reciprocal-scale hypothesis preserved.
